subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: if two figures are congruent, which two things are the same?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: agar do figures congruent hain, toh kaunsi do cheezein same hain?
answer: Shape and size

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two triangles have sides 7 cm and 9 cm with a 40° angle between them in both. Congruent? Which rule?
prompt_hi: Do triangles mein 7 cm aur 9 cm ki sides hain aur dono mein unke beech 40° ka angle hai. Congruent? Kaunsa rule?
answer: Yes, by SAS

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two triangles each have angles 60° and 45° with a 5 cm side between them. Congruent? Which rule?
prompt_hi: Do triangles mein 60° aur 45° ke angle hain aur unke beech 5 cm ki side. Congruent? Kaunsa rule?
answer: Yes, by ASA

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two right triangles each have hypotenuse 13 cm and one other side 5 cm. Congruent? Which rule?
prompt_hi: Do right triangles ka hypotenuse 13 cm aur ek aur side 5 cm hai. Congruent? Kaunsa rule?
answer: Yes, by RHS (the third side is 12 cm in both)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict: if you and a friend each draw a triangle with angles 30°, 60° and 90°, will your triangles be congruent? Then compare.
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: tum aur tumhara dost dono 30°, 60° aur 90° wala triangle banao, toh kya dono congruent honge? Phir compare karo.
answer: Probably not: the shape is the same but the sizes can differ; equal angles do not fix the size

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare SAS and SSA: both use two sides and an angle. What is the difference, and which one works?
prompt_hi: SAS aur SSA ko compare karo: dono mein do sides aur ek angle hai. Farak kya hai, aur kaunsa kaam karta hai?
answer: In SAS the angle is between the two sides, and it works; in SSA it is not, and two different triangles can be made, so it does not work

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why are bridge frames and electricity towers made of triangles, not squares?
prompt_hi: Pul ke frame aur bijli ke tower triangle se kyun bante hain, square se kyun nahi?
answer: By SSS, once its three sides are fixed a triangle cannot change shape (it is rigid); a square with fixed sides can still squash into a rhombus

subject: maths
prompt_en: Sameer says two triangles with angles 40°, 60° and 80° must be congruent. Check his claim.
prompt_hi: Sameer kehta hai 40°, 60° aur 80° wale do triangle zaroor congruent hain. Uski baat check karo.
answer: Wrong: equal angles only give the same shape; one triangle can be an enlarged copy, so AAA is not a congruence rule

subject: maths
prompt_en: In ΔABC and ΔPQR, AB = QR, BC = RP and CA = PQ. Nisha wrote ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR. Fix her statement.
prompt_hi: ΔABC aur ΔPQR mein AB = QR, BC = RP aur CA = PQ. Nisha ne ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR likha. Uska statement theek karo.
answer: ΔABC ≅ ΔQRP (A ↔ Q, B ↔ R, C ↔ P)

subject: maths
prompt_en: A flying kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. Show that triangles ABC and ADC are congruent.
prompt_hi: Ek patang ABCD mein AB = AD aur CB = CD hai. Dikhao ki triangle ABC aur ADC congruent hain.
answer: AB = AD, CB = CD and AC is shared, so ΔABC ≅ ΔADC by SSS

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two surveyors check two triangular plots. Two angles of the first plot match two angles of the second. They can measure only one side of each plot. Does it matter which side they measure, as long as it is the matching side in both plots? Explain.
prompt_hi: Do surveyor do triangle wale plot check kar rahe hain. Pehle plot ke do angle doosre plot ke do angle se match karte hain. Woh har plot ki sirf ek side naap sakte hain. Kya isse farak padta hai ki kaunsi side naapein, agar dono plots mein matching side hi naapein? Samjhao.
answer: It does not matter: any matching side works. The third angles are equal too (angle sum is 180°), so all three angles match, and any side then lies between two matching angles, giving ASA (the included side directly, or AAS for another side)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Describe how to draw two different triangles that both have sides 6 cm and 4 cm and a 30° angle that is not between those sides.
prompt_hi: Batao ki aise do alag triangle kaise banaoge jinki sides 6 cm aur 4 cm hon aur ek 30° ka angle ho jo un sides ke beech na ho.
answer: Draw a 30° angle at A and make AB = 6 cm along one arm; a 4 cm arc from B cuts the other arm at two points, giving two different triangles (one wide, one narrow)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend the four congruence rules for triangles and one set of facts that does NOT work.
prompt_hi: Dost ko triangles ke chaar congruence rule sikhao aur ek aisi jaankari jo kaam NAHI karti.
answer: SSS, SAS (angle between the sides), ASA (side between the angles) and RHS; AAA (and SSA) do not work

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: what do the letters RHS stand for?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: RHS ke letters ka matlab kya hai?
answer: Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side

subject: maths
prompt_en: What is each angle of an equilateral triangle?
prompt_hi: Equilateral triangle ka har angle kitna hota hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: In an isosceles triangle the apex angle is 50°. Find each base angle.
prompt_hi: Isosceles triangle ka apex angle 50° hai. Har base angle nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: In an isosceles triangle each base angle is 70°. Find the apex angle.
prompt_hi: Isosceles triangle ka har base angle 70° hai. Apex angle nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: An A-frame roof has two equal sloping sides. Predict: if the left roof angle with the floor is 55°, what is the right one? Then check with the angle sum.
prompt_hi: A-frame chhat ki do dhalaan wali sides barabar hain. Andaaza lagao: agar baayi taraf ka angle zameen se 55° hai, toh daayi taraf ka kitna? Phir angle sum se check karo.
answer: 55°: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal (the top angle is 70°)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare a triangle with sides 6, 6, 6 and one with sides 6, 6, 4. What can you say about the angles of each?
prompt_hi: 6, 6, 6 wale triangle ko 6, 6, 4 wale se compare karo. Dono ke angles ke baare mein kya keh sakte ho?
answer: 6, 6, 6: all three angles are 60°; 6, 6, 4: only the two base angles (opposite the 6 cm sides) are equal

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why are the base angles of an isosceles triangle equal? Use congruent triangles.
prompt_hi: Isosceles triangle ke base angles barabar kyun hote hain? Congruent triangles se samjhao.
answer: Join the apex to the midpoint of the base: the two halves have the equal sides, equal half-bases and a shared line, so they are congruent by SSS and the base angles match

subject: maths
prompt_en: In ΔABC with AB = AC, Rohit marked angle A = angle B. Check him.
prompt_hi: ΔABC mein AB = AC hai, aur Rohit ne angle A = angle B likha. Use check karo.
answer: Wrong: the equal angles are opposite the equal sides, so angle B (opposite AC) = angle C (opposite AB)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Kavya says an isosceles triangle can't have a 100° angle 'because isosceles means pointy'. Is she right?
prompt_hi: Kavya kehti hai isosceles triangle mein 100° ka angle nahi ho sakta 'kyunki isosceles matlab nukeela'. Kya woh sahi hai?
answer: No: angles 100°, 40°, 40° make an isosceles obtuse triangle

subject: maths
prompt_en: An isosceles triangle has a 90° angle. Find the other two angles.
prompt_hi: Ek isosceles triangle mein 90° ka angle hai. Baaki do angle nikaalo.
answer: 45° each

subject: maths
prompt_en: A hill-house roof truss is an isosceles triangle with a 110° angle at the top. The carpenter cuts the beam ends to fit the base angles. What angle should each cut be?
prompt_hi: Pahaadi ghar ki chhat ka truss isosceles triangle hai jiska upar ka angle 110° hai. Badhai beam ke siron ko base angles ke hisaab se kaatta hai. Har cut kitne angle ka ho?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Fold a paper isosceles triangle so the two equal sides lie on each other. What does the crease show about the base angles?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz ke isosceles triangle ko aise modo ki do barabar sides ek doosre par aa jaayein. Crease base angles ke baare mein kya dikhati hai?
answer: The base angles land exactly on each other, so they are equal; the crease is the line of symmetry from the apex to the base's midpoint

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to find all the angles of an isosceles triangle when only the apex angle is given.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki sirf apex angle diya ho toh isosceles triangle ke saare angle kaise nikaalte hain.
answer: Subtract the apex angle from 180°, then halve the result, because the two base angles are equal

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: in an isosceles triangle, which angles are equal?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: isosceles triangle mein kaunse angle barabar hote hain?
answer: The two angles opposite the equal sides (the base angles)

subject: maths
prompt_en: What is (−6) × 4?
prompt_hi: (−6) × 4 kitna hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Show 3 × (−2) as jumps on a number line starting at 0. Where do you land?
prompt_hi: 3 × (−2) ko number line par 0 se jumps karke dikhao. Kahan pahunchoge?
answer: Three jumps of 2 to the left: 0 → −2 → −4 → −6, landing at −6

subject: maths
answer: 2: the products go up by 2 each step, so after 0 comes 2

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why is (−1) × (−5) positive and not negative?
prompt_hi: (−1) × (−5) positive kyun hai, negative kyun nahi?
answer: Following the pattern 2 × (−5) = −10, 1 × (−5) = −5, 0 × (−5) = 0, each step goes up by 5, so (−1) × (−5) = 5; multiplying by −1 flips −5 to its opposite

subject: maths
prompt_hi: (−7) × (−8) kitna hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare (−4) + (−6) and (−4) × (−6). Are both positive?
prompt_hi: (−4) + (−6) aur (−4) × (−6) ko compare karo. Kya dono positive hain?
answer: No: (−4) + (−6) = −10, but (−4) × (−6) = 24; 'two negatives make a positive' is only for multiplying

subject: maths
prompt_en: Tanu worked out (−2) × (−5) × (−3) = 30, saying 'negatives make positive'. Check her.
prompt_hi: Tanu ne (−2) × (−5) × (−3) = 30 nikala, bolke 'negatives milke positive'. Check karo.
answer: Wrong: −30; there are three negative factors, the first two make +10 and then × (−3) gives −30

subject: maths
prompt_en: The temperature falls 3 °C every hour. What is the total change in 5 hours?
prompt_hi: Taapmaan har ghante 3 °C girta hai. 5 ghante mein kul kitna badlav hoga?

subject: maths
prompt_en: A shopkeeper loses ₹40 on each of 6 damaged umbrellas and gains ₹25 on each of 10 umbrellas sold. Write it with integers. Profit or loss overall?
prompt_hi: Ek dukaandaar ko 6 kharab chhataon par har ek par ₹40 ka nuksaan aur 10 bechi chhataon par har ek par ₹25 ka munafa hua. Integers se likho. Kul munafa ya nuksaan?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict the sign: (−1) multiplied by itself 7 times. Then say the answer.
prompt_hi: Sign ka andaaza lagao: (−1) ko khud se 7 baar multiply karo. Phir answer batao.
answer: −1: seven negative factors is an odd number, so the product is negative

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend the sign rules for multiplying integers, with one example each.
prompt_hi: Dost ko integers multiply karne ke sign rules sikhao, har ek ka ek example dekar.
answer: Same signs give a positive product (e.g. (−2) × (−3) = 6); different signs give a negative product (e.g. 2 × (−3) = −6); count negatives for longer products

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick one from memory: (−9) × (−3) = ?
prompt_hi: Yaad se jaldi batao: (−9) × (−3) = ?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Someone says (−3) × 0 = −3. Check.
prompt_hi: Kisi ne kaha (−3) × 0 = −3. Check karo.
answer: Wrong: anything multiplied by 0 is 0
